instructions.content: Prefer the semantic-scholar MCP, then the google-scholar MCP, over WebFetch for paper discovery and metadata; fall back to WebFetch on the arxiv abstract page only when neither is configured or returns results.
Resolve the source by input type: arxiv ID or URL via the MCP, DOI via the MCP rather than a raw HTTP fetch, and a PDF path by reading the file.
Derive a stable slug of the form <firstauthor-surname>-<2-3 word topic>.
Check REVIEWED.md and references/REFERENCE_INDEX.md for the slug or arxiv ID; if already present, report it and stop.
Classify the paper with one or more tags: survey, benchmark, empirical, theoretical, system.
Read assets/templates/REFERENCE-paper.yaml and create references/<slug>.md with all required frontmatter fields followed by the required sections.
Populate every section: TL;DR with 3 to 8 bullets, What's novel, Mechanism overview (N/A where not applicable), Evaluation, Implementation details worth stealing, Open questions.
Quote all numbers with their source and mark evaluation results (as reported).
Add a REVIEWED.md summary row (reverse-chronological) and a detailed section with disposition pending.
Add a REFERENCE_INDEX.md row under the most relevant category, noting it for the user if no category fits.
Report what was created, then offer the user a choice: promote, keep in REVIEWED.md, or skip with reasoning.
When the user confirms promotion, create analysis/ANALYSIS-arxiv-<id>-<slug>.md from assets/templates/ANALYSIS-paper.yaml and change the REVIEWED.md disposition from pending to analysis.
Validate completed files with scripts/validate-reference-paper.sh and scripts/validate-analysis-paper.sh.
NEVER omit YAML frontmatter; open every file with a --- block containing all required fields.
NEVER invent benchmark numbers; mark them (as reported) with their source.
NEVER skip the duplicate check before creating files.
NEVER promote to ANALYSIS-*.md without user confirmation.
Quote what the paper reports as evidence first; never infer or embellish claims.
If a paper is tangentially related, triage it and flag it; do not silently skip it.
Do not use this skill for a paper already triaged, a paper clearly out of scope, or a full deep dive (triage first, then promote).
